선생님.e: Literally 'born before' + 님 (honorific) — someone who is ahead of you.
선생님.t: Also a respectful title for doctors and other professionals. Use honorific verbs: 선생님이 오세요.

안방.x: My parents usually sleep in the master bedroom.
안방.e: Native 안 (inner) + 방 (room); traditionally the inner room of the lady of the house.

다녀왔습니다.ex: 엄마, 학교 다녀왔습니다! 오늘 정말 배고파요.
다녀왔습니다.x: Mom, I'm home from school! I'm really hungry today.
다녀왔습니다.e: Past form of 다녀오다 'go and come back': literally 'I went and came back'.

이상하다.m: to be strange, to be weird, to be odd
이상하다.x: This milk tastes a little strange.
이상하다.t: Don't confuse it with 이상 'more than' or 이상 'ideal' — same sound, different words.

짬뽕.e: Probably from Japanese 'champon', a Nagasaki noodle dish; the Korean version became red and spicy.
짬뽕.t: 짜장면 or 짬뽕 is a classic dilemma, so some places sell 짬짜면, half of each. Casually, 짬뽕 also means 'a jumble, a mix'.

수입하다.x: Our company imports wine from France.
수입하다.t: Don't mix it up with the homonym 수입 meaning 'income' — context tells you which one is meant.

다양하다.x: This market sells a variety of foods.

지각.x: I overslept and was late for work today.
지각.t: Homonym warning: 지각 (知覺) also means 'perception', but 'lateness' is far more common.

지각.ex: 사람마다 색에 대한 지각이 조금씩 달라요.
지각.x: Each person's perception of color is slightly different.
지각.t: Homonym: 지각 'being late' is far more common in daily life — 학교에 지각했어요.

대상.ex: 이 영어 프로그램은 초등학생을 대상으로 합니다.
대상.x: This English program is aimed at elementary school students.
대상.e: Literally 'the image you face' — whatever something is aimed at.
대상.t: Key pattern: N을/를 대상으로 'aimed at N, for N' — very common in notices.

변경하다.m: to change, to alter, to modify
변경하다.x: To change your password, press this button.
변경하다.t: 변경하다 is notice-style; in conversation, 바꾸다 sounds more natural.

신곡.x: As soon as the new song came out, it hit number one on the music charts.
신곡.t: 곡 is the formal word and counter for songs: 이번 앨범에는 열 곡이 있어요.

고용주.ex: 고용주는 직원에게 최저 임금 이상을 줘야 해요.
고용주.x: Employers must pay workers at least the minimum wage.

이직하다.m: to change jobs, to move to another company
이직하다.ex: 저는 작년에 연봉이 더 높은 회사로 이직했어요.
이직하다.x: Last year I moved to a company with a higher salary.
이직하다.t: 이직 means switching companies; 전근 means moving offices within the same company.

기업가.ex: 그는 젊은 나이에 성공한 기업가가 되었어요.
기업가.x: He became a successful entrepreneur at a young age.
기업가.e: -가 = professional or expert: 기업가, 작가, 전문가.
기업가.t: Pronounced [기업까]; a 기업가 founds or runs a business, while a 회사원 is an employee.

떠맡다.m: to take on, to be saddled with (a task)
떠맡다.ex: 동료가 휴가를 가서 제가 그 일을 떠맡았어요.
떠맡다.x: My coworker went on vacation, so I got stuck with the work.
떠맡다.e: Built on 맡다 'to take charge'; suggests a job pushed onto you.

꿀팁.ex: 자취생을 위한 요리 꿀팁 좀 알려 주세요.
꿀팁.x: Please share some cooking tips for people living alone.
꿀팁.e: 꿀 'honey' + English 'tip'; slang 꿀- means 'sweet, great'.
꿀팁.t: Casual. The same 꿀- appears in 꿀잼 'super fun' and 꿀잠 'sweet sleep'.

혼밥.x: I had lunch alone at a restaurant near the office.
혼밥.t: Casual. Korean meals were traditionally shared, so eating alone used to feel awkward; now it's common, and many places have counter seats or one-person menus for 혼밥족 'solo diners'.

전력난.ex: 한여름에는 에어컨 사용으로 전력난이 생기기도 해요.
전력난.x: In midsummer, power shortages sometimes occur because of air conditioner use.
전력난.t: Pronounced [절령난] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ, then ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㄴ.

느닷없이.m: suddenly, out of nowhere, without warning
느닷없이.ex: 친구가 느닷없이 집에 찾아와서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
느닷없이.x: My friend showed up at my house out of nowhere, and I was startled.
느닷없이.e: Ends in 없이 'without' — think 'without any warning'.

꼬박.forms: 꼬박 + time span (꼬박 하루, 꼬박 3년) · 밤을 꼬박 새우다
꼬박.ex: 시험 공부 때문에 밤을 꼬박 새웠어요.
꼬박.x: I stayed up the whole night studying for the exam.
꼬박.e: Base of 꼬박꼬박 'regularly, without missing once'.
꼬박.t: Key collocation: 밤을 꼬박 새우다 'to stay up all night'.

이정표.ex: 이번 협정은 두 나라 관계에 중요한 이정표가 되었습니다.
이정표.x: This agreement became an important milestone in the two countries' relations.
이정표.e: Literally 'journey-distance marker': a roadside stone showing distances.
이정표.t: Often used figuratively with 되다 or 세우다: 새로운 이정표를 세우다 (set a new milestone).

투정.x: My little brother whined that the side dishes didn't taste good.

사법.ex: 사법 개혁에 대한 국민의 요구가 커지고 있습니다.
사법.x: Public demand for judicial reform is growing.
사법.e: Literally 'administering the law'; a homonym 사법 means 'private law'.
사법.t: It pairs with 입법 and 행정 as the three branches; 사법부 means 'the judicial branch'.

비정부기구.x: Several NGOs provided food to the refugees.
비정부기구.e: Literally 'non-government organization', a direct translation of NGO.
비정부기구.t: In speech, many Koreans simply say 엔지오 (NGO).

여백의 미.forms: 여백의 미를 살리다 · 여백의 미가 느껴지다
여백의 미.m: beauty of empty space, aesthetic of restraint
여백의 미.ex: 한국 전통 그림은 여백의 미를 잘 살려요.
여백의 미.x: Traditional Korean paintings make good use of the beauty of empty space.
여백의 미.e: A key idea in Korean aesthetics: what's left empty matters as much as what's painted.
여백의 미.t: Used beyond art, too — for design, architecture, even a simply decorated room.

조성.ex: 현대 음악 중에는 조성이 없는 곡도 많아요.
조성.x: Many modern pieces have no tonality at all.
조성.e: Homonym alert: 조성 more often means 'creating', as in 공원 조성.

관직.ex: 그는 관직에서 물러나 고향에서 책을 썼어요.
관직.x: He retired from office and wrote books in his hometown.

수령.x: The magistrate governed the provinces on behalf of the king.
수령.e: Literally 'one who guards and commands' a district.
수령.t: Homonyms: 수령 also means receiving (a package) and a gang leader, each with different characters.

질박하다.ex: 이 도자기는 질박한 아름다움을 지니고 있어요.
질박하다.x: This pottery has a plain, unadorned beauty.
질박하다.e: Literally 'all substance, plainly made' — beauty without decoration.

시종.ex: 그는 인터뷰 동안 시종 진지한 태도를 보였어요.
시종.x: He kept a serious attitude from start to finish during the interview.

의당.m: naturally, rightly, as a matter of course
의당.x: If you did something wrong, you naturally ought to apologize.

상호작용.ex: 아이들은 친구와의 상호작용을 통해 많이 배웁니다.
상호작용.x: Children learn a lot through interaction with friends.

도청도설.ex: 인터넷에 떠도는 도청도설을 그대로 믿으면 안 됩니다.
도청도설.x: You shouldn't believe the hearsay floating around online.
도청도설.e: Literally 'heard on the road, repeated on the road'.
도청도설.t: Don't confuse with 도청 'wiretapping', which is written with different characters.
